verdict.rationale: Clerky has programmatic surfaces: a Partner API for formation document sets and an OAuth-gated, read-only MCP server. So automation depth is a fair question, but nothing in the evidence describes user-defined automations that can be versioned, reviewed, or rolled back. The document-set change log (who changed what) and the attorney review/comment features apply to legal documents, not automations, so they are adjacent features that earn no credit.
